images.caption: Ben Nevis, 1,344 metres, Scotland. Photograph taken from Banavie about 8 km north west. 18:55, 11 July 2005.  The summit is beyond and to the left of the apparent highest point, Càrn Dearg North, 1,221 metres, (many Scottish mountains are called Càrn Dearg). Càrn Mòr Dearg, 1,223 metres, is to the left, connected to the Ben by the Càrn Mòr Dearg Arête at the head of Coire Leis (slightly in shadow). The pipelines of the Lochaber hydroelectric scheme are visible lower right.

images.caption:
Constable Simon MacDonald joined the force in May 1902 and was transerred that September to Fort William, and then in 1904 he moved again to Onich, south of Fort William. 
He later moved to Foyers (1912) and was then posted to Cannich in 1913 where he remained until 1920 when moving to Stoneybrige on the Isle of South Uist for the remarkably brief period of a year before returning to Drumnadrochit - where he remained for 14 years till he retired on pension. 
His grandson also subsequently served as beat officer at Cannich.

Date and location of this photograph are uncertain but I suspect it was during his period at Onich, as this card was in the same bundle of papers as the 1906 "Locheil Welcome Arch" one.

images.caption:
One of the most famous waterways in the world. 
I've driven alongside it many times but never seen anything of "Nessie" the monster.  Whether or not the beast exists there is no doubt the legend is good for the shopkeepers and hotels. Having said that there are many other scenic attractions in the area for those disappointed by no sighting.

The loch is 22 miles long and up to one and a half miles wide. It's unusually deep - up to 745 feet, 227 metres - and has the largest volume of water anywhere inland in the British Isles.

images.filename: Armed Forces Day - Parade to Inverness Highland Games 2012 Scotland (Massed Pipe Bands) (7618399252).jpg
images.caption:
The Massed Bands play round the arena at Northern Meeting Park during the City of Inverness Highland Games.
As in several previous years, the Armed Forces Day and Parade was incorporated into the City of Inverness Highland Games.
Massed Pipe Bands formed up in Falcon Square and then proceeded to lead the Colours and parade from Eastgate through Inverness City Centre, to the Northern Meeting Park where the Highland Games was to take place. The Games then began with a Drumhead Service and Presentation of Veterans Medals.
The Massed Pipe Bands were under the command of Drum Major David Murray (BW, Ret) and comprised pipes and drums from:
- Northern Constabulary PB
- Inverness Royal British Legion PB
- Queens Own Highlanders Association PB
- Forres PB 
- Sutherland Caledonian PB
- Isle of Skye PB.

The weather was gorgeous for this memorable event, made all the more poignant by the absence of the man who organised the event these past few years (including this year), Pipe Major Denis Swanson of the Inverness Royal British Legion Pipe Band, who sadly passed away earlier this year.
